腕.meaning: A postman is handed a letter whose <part>address</part> just says 'The Man in the <part>Moon</part>'. No rocket, no ladder, so he rolls up his sleeve and reaches up, past the clouds and the satellites, and pops it through the moon's letterbox. That's one long <kanji>arm</kanji>.
腕.on: Back at the sorting office he arm-wrestles everyone, and he has <sound>won</sound> every match since.
腕.kun: He slurps a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, then reaches across town to pass it to his <sound>de</sound>ntist.

握.meaning: A storm hits the harbour, and the little corner <part>shop</part> starts sliding toward the sea. The shopkeeper hurls a ship's <part>anchor</part> out the door, it hooks a bollard, and he hangs on with both hands as the till rolls past his feet. He never loosens his <kanji>grip</kanji>.
握.on: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' cries the <sound>coo</sound>k from the café next door, clinging to his frying pan.
握.kun: His fist is so tight that the sewing <sound>nee</sound>dle and the bike <sound>gea</sound>r he was holding get squashed flat.

致.meaning: An old-fashioned actor climbs onto a podium, flicks open a lace fan and declares, 'Thou art late, and the king doth frown!' He talks like this at the shops, at the dentist, at bedtime. Whatever he does, he doth.
致.on: Only a <sound>chee</sound>tah in the front row claps, very fast.
致.kun: 'I shall humbly do the washing up,' he bows, then squeals '<sound>Ee</sound>!' at a <sound>ta</sound>co stuck to the pan.

封.meaning: A pirate buries his letters under a <part>double mound</part> of sand, then whacks the top flat with a <part>golf club</part> so nobody can dig. A walrus flops down on top and refuses to budge. That's the best <kanji>seal</kanji> he could wish for.
封.on: He closes his lunch box just as tight, so no gull can steal his <sound>foo</sound>d.

騒.meaning: At a garden party, a <part>horse</part> is munching a giant <part>pretzel</part> when an <part>insect</part> crawls into his ear. He bucks, neighs, kicks over the punch bowl and gallops round the lawn with the band chasing him. It's the most <kanji>boisterous</kanji> party of the year.
騒.on: Someone slips on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and slides under the table, giggling.
騒.kun: The guests dance to loud <sound>sa</sound>lsa and yell '<sound>Wah</sound>!' until the neighbours bang on the wall.

侵.meaning: Your roommate hangs his coat on your <part>coat hook</part>. Next day his <part>rake</part> leans in your corner, then his <part>blanket</part> creeps onto your bed, and a half-eaten <part>pretzel</part> turns up on your pillow. Inch by inch, his stuff starts to <kanji>encroach</kanji>.
侵.on: One night you stub your <sound>shin</sound> on his rake in the dark.
侵.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you yell, and chop his pretzel in half with a <sound>ka</sound>rate chop.

旧.meaning: When the town gets bright new street lamps, the old paper <part>sun</part> from the school play is nailed to a <part>pole</part> in the square. Every evening the grandpas gather under it, squinting fondly at its peeling paint and talking about the <kanji>old times</kanji>.
旧.on: They argue over who was best at pool, waving a chipped <sound>cue</sound> at the paper sun.
旧.kun: One snoozes on a <sound>fu</sound>ton under the pole while a <sound>roo</sound>k pecks at the peeling paint.

揺.meaning: In a storm, the ship's cook hangs his lucky <part>can opener</part> from the <part>anchor</part> chain above the galley. Back and forth it goes, like a hypnotist's watch, until the whole crew is snoring in time to its <kanji>swing</kanji>.
揺.on: Only the captain stays awake, doing tricks with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo that dips in time with it.
揺.kun: A <sound>yu</sound>zu rolls from one side of the deck to the other as the ship sways.

詰.meaning: A best man has an hour-long <part>speech</part> and only one tiny <part>good luck</part> card to write it on. He shrinks his handwriting until every word fits, edge to edge, up the sides and round the stamp. The card is <kanji>packed</kanji>.
詰.on: He reads it out through a magnifying glass while a <sound>kit</sound>ten bats at the card.
詰.kun: Then he sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and tiny words fly off the crowded card.
